housing.summary: Manchester's rental market is competitive, especially in the city centre and areas like Ancoats, Northern Quarter, and Salford Quays. Tenancies are typically Assured Shorthold Tenancies (AST), commonly 12 months. Landlords/agents usually require referencing, proof of income, and a security deposit protected in a government-approved scheme.

banking.summary: Opening a UK current account generally requires proof of identity and proof of UK address. Newcomers can use high-street banks or app-based banks (which often accept fewer documents). Some banks offer accounts geared toward new arrivals without a long address history.
required_docs: Proof of UK address (utility bill, tenancy agreement, or bank letter)
Proof of employment or visa/BRP where applicable

schools.summary: State schooling in Manchester is free and allocated by catchment/admissions criteria via the local authority. Independent and international options exist for families wanting alternative curricula. Applications for state school places go through Manchester City Council admissions.

legal_admin.summary: The UK has no continental-style residential registration. Newcomers typically confirm status via a Biometric Residence Permit (BRP) or eVisa, register with a local GP, and apply for a National Insurance Number for work. Address is evidenced through tenancy and utility documents rather than a civil registry.
legal_admin.registration_step: Register with a local GP surgery and apply for a National Insurance Number; confirm immigration status via BRP/eVisa where applicable

tax_finance.summary: Income tax and National Insurance are administered by HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), generally deducted at source through PAYE for employees. New workers should obtain a National Insurance Number and may need to verify their tax code with HMRC.

transport.summary: Manchester is served by an integrated network of Metrolink trams, buses (now under the Bee Network franchising), and local/regional rail. Contactless and capped fares are widely available. Season tickets and travelcards cover tram/bus zones across Greater Manchester.
transport.network_name: Transport for Greater Manchester (Metrolink / Bee Network)
transport.driving_licence_exchange: Many overseas licences can be used for up to 12 months; some countries' licences can be exchanged for a UK licence via the DVLA, others require passing a UK driving test.
transport.healthcare_registration: Register with a local NHS GP surgery to access primary healthcare; the Immigration Health Surcharge (paid with most visas) grants NHS access.
